requirement:
Each documented annotation exposes its current tracked justification
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`
and its last recorded review under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.reviews`.
Missing justification and missing or unreadable stored reviews are
distinguished.
rationale: I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request any implementation source. **Obligations derived from `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.explanations`:** 1. Each documented annotation shows its current tracked justification. That covers fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments, and the justification must follow source edits. 2. Each annotation shows its last recorded review. 3. A missing justification is distinguished from a present one. 4. A missing stored review is distinguished from an unreadable one. The detailed rendering rules sit in the cited `notes.justifications` and `notes.reviews` requirements. I treated those as context and did not reassess their tests. **Test mapping:** - `documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`: - It builds a file-root fenced citation ("Root explanation."), function fenced citations ("First/Second explanation.") and a Rust doc comment ("Function explanation."). - It also builds an annotation with no justification. - It asserts each card contains the right explanation text. The unexplained item gets "No tracked justification is present." - It asserts the item location and selector strings, such as `File root` and `fn[one]`. - It asserts "Recorded review:" is present. - `overview_shows_missing_unreadable_and_recorded_reviews_with_current_justifications` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`: - It loops over review states: missing, recorded true, false, FIXME, invalid JSON, and an unreadable path (a directory in place of the file). - It asserts the exact labels `Recorded review: Missing`, `Recorded true`, `Recorded false`, `Recorded FIXME` and `Unreadable`. These assertions are what distinguish missing from unreadable. - It asserts the saved rationale appears for readable reviews, and the FIXME text appears for FIXME. - It asserts the failure explanations "invalid JSON" and "cannot read evidence". - It then edits the source and checks the justification is current. The old explanation disappears. "Updated platform explanation." appears, or "No tracked justification is present." when the doc comment is removed. The recorded review stays displayed and the review file is byte-identical. - `book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements` in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`: - It is an end-to-end render. It checks Missing, then true, false and FIXME reviews, alongside the doc-comment justification. - After the source changes, it checks "No tracked justification is present." together with "Recorded true". **Gaps:** I found none. Each clause is exercised and asserted. The assertions include negative cases (stale explanation gone, no "current and accepted" wording). Missing and unreadable reviews are asserted with different labels, and the missing-justification case is asserted. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} index.gaps.explanations
Each documented annotation exposes its current tracked justification
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`
and its last recorded review under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.reviews`.
Missing justification and missing or unreadable stored reviews are
distinguished.
:::{req} index.file_map.notes.justifications
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.
File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
:::{req} index.file_map.notes.reviews
Each coverage annotation shows its last recorded citation-review
determination and rationale when readable. It distinguishes a missing review
from an unreadable review and explains failures to read the record.
Recorded results are labeled as recorded reviews; rendering does not check
whether they are current or authorize an execution-coverage exception.
